text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Support for the governing Social Democratic Party has increased to 26.7 percent, it is now ahead of opposition Centre Party with 20.5 percent, poll shows.
- Jobless try to save money by cutting down on cosmetics and healthy food, but their alcohol and tobacco consumption is still higher than that of working people, statistics show.

- In the late 1960s ane early 1970s, the late President Urho Kekkonen suggested to the Soviet Union that parts of Finnish Lapland could be swapped for the Finnish city Viipuri, ceded to the Soviets at end of the Second World War, says Kekkonen's biographer Juhani Suomi.
- Immigrant candidates in the municipal elections are unanimous in observing that unemployment is the biggest obstacle to foreigners' adjustment to Finnish society.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Swedes congratulate themselves on fending off ERM.
- Finnair planning to set up cargo centre in Singapore to bolster its position in air freight between Nordic countries and Asia.
- Finland moving quickly towards on-line and even wireless banking. Further pruning of bank branch network lies ahead, one banker says.

- Finnish futures brokers Suomen Optiomeklarit Oy and Swedish counterpart OM Stockholm AB plan to open their electronic trading systems to each others' members -- goal is a joint Nordic derivatives market.
DEMARI
- Speaker of Parliament rejected Centre Party's call for an emergency session of parliament to discuss Finland joining ERM.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Metsa-Rauma's new mill, the world's biggest single-lined softwood pulp mill, is now up to production speed and staffed by just 180 workers.
- Finnair in service partnerships with Alitalia on Milan route and with Sabena on Brussels and Geneva routes.
- Agriculture Minister Kalevi Hemila welcomes EU decision to recognise Baltic herring as a real fish.
- Small 3.1 Richter scale earthquake shook Ylitornio area in far north at weekend.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish army officers surprised at inflexible decision-making in NATO Baltic circle Partnership for Peace exercises.
